decision.reason: Measured maximum stable enqueue CPU saving near 34 microseconds is too small to explain the reported FPS regression; defer complexity and prioritize the pacing/render-filter work.

methods.round_order: interleaved; queue variant order rotated each round

preparation.timed: native geometry construction, packet replay, renderer state work; actual geometry/rectangle draw calls replaced by counters

software.timed: render_host_layers + SDL_RenderFlush; software raster included; clear outside timer

queue.timed: render_host_layers; actual SDL API calls and queue processing included; SDL_RenderFlush timed separately
queue.deferred_write_proof: A surface pixel is unchanged after rendering and changes only after explicit flush

methods.aggregation: median of three per-round CPU medians; per-round medians retained

exact_pixel_comparisons.method: full normalized RGBA byte comparison, not a visual tolerance or alpha-only bbox check

public_reproduction_harness.scope: baseline real enqueue/flush diagnostic; candidates remain private

smoke_validation.stderr: PASS SDL window software batching defers actual surface writes until flush

limitations: CPU results from x86_64 SDL software do not measure Android CPU or GPU time.
SDL GLES2 merges compatible consecutive geometry commands: SDL API call counts are not GPU drawcall counts.
Preparation counter experiment deliberately excludes SDL geometry queue validation and rasterization.
Full software-raster differences are small and not uniform across cases.
Candidate key invalidation and renderer lifetime were not broadly certified because candidates are not integrated.
Existing control hit-region implementation was untouched; no new Android gesture or device FPS claim.
